newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ASEAN foreign ministers to meet Sihanouk Thursday.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN foreign ministers to meet Sihanouk Thursday.

text.p: Three ASEAN foreign ministers will meet King Norodom Sihanouk in Beijing on Thursday to seek a solution to the Cambodian crisis, Indonesia's Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
Spokesman Ghaffar Fadyl said Indonesia's Ali Alatas would leave for the Chinese capital on Wednesday night and meet up with the Thai and Philippines foreign ministers there.

A special meeting of foreign ministers of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) agreed in Kuala Lumpur last week to postpone Cambodia's entry into the seven-nation grouping as a result of the turmoil in the country.
Cambodia, together with Burma and Laos, had been due to join ASEAN at its 30th anniversary meeting in the Malaysian capital late this month. The other two are expected to join as scheduled.
ASEAN currently comprises Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam and Brunei.

The ministers at last week's meeting expressed concern at the situation in Cambodia and urged an immediate ceasefire between warring supporters of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, Sihanouk's son, and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.

They mandated Alatas and foreign ministers Prachuab Chaiyasarn of Thailand and Domingo Siazon of the Philippines to meet Sihanouk -- in Beijing for medical treatment -- to try to promote a negotiated settlement.
Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh on July 6 and has said Cambodia might reconsider its planned membership in ASEAN if the group interfered in his country's internal affairs.
Alatas has denied that ASEAN had this intention. ASEAN said last week it still recognised Ranariddh as first prime minister.

Sihanouk said on Monday he doubted whether efforts by ASEAN, along with France, Japan and the United States, would succeed in bringing a negotiated settlement to the Cambodian crisis in light of Hun Sen's earlier rejection of an earlier offer to hold reconciliation talks.
But he said he was willing to meet the ASEAN envoys.
